utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, yesterday I was asking you questions about exchanges, and discussion amongst prisoners on how to bring about the exchange, and you answered that, in reply to a question regarding that there was an agreement that it was a particular way to bring it about, you said: "Mostly those who had money, they were exchanged." Do you have any information as to whom they paid money in order to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information regarding that. All I know pertains to myself. I gave to the commander of the camp, Djoko Pajic, 500 German marks to exchange me. However, I didn't do that and later on he was replaced. Now he's living in Bijeljina. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking about yourself. I'm asking about others. Do you have any information, anything that you heard from others, other prisoners, other men who were detained with you as to whom payment was to occur?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what, there's always information circulating, but they're frequently informal, so I really couldn't tell you anything about who accepted money, when people were exchanged. I don't know that. I was in the camp, as you say yourself, and certain people from the camp were exchanged, but I didn't know anything about it while in the camp. There were very strict rules in the camp. We couldn't talk among each other frequently, we couldn't walk around. We had strict rules regarding when we were allowed to go to the toilet and when we went to drink water. It was all at specific times of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, do you know a gentleman named Emin Gebic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Son of Hasib.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was he in custody with you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he exchanged?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you how he went about getting or securing his exchange?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was exchanged and went to Orasje. I didn't keep in contact with him. He didn't tell me anything in detail about giving money or somebody accepting money. But there are many rumours, but what can I tell you? Rumours and rumours and acts are acts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness, yesterday and today, said that he did not have direct information, so I don't know why is the Prosecutor insisting on this. The witness has confirmed once again that he has no direct knowledge, and I don't think that this should be repeated or insisted on, because the witness was quite clear on this matter. MR. DI FAZIO: I've gone as as far as I can on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. Let's move on. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's just return to the issue of your property and we'll wrap up this examination-in-chief. You said -- I just want to re-establish two things relating to your home. You said yesterday that this man, Stevanovic, came along to the camp and that you signed that document giving him a power of attorney and that you did so because, naturally enough, you felt under very considerable pressure. That is so, is it not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Using that power of attorney, he dealt with and disposed of your property; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You had to initiate legal proceedings in order to recover that property; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have had some success in doing so, but not complete success yet?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to establish in respect of the property. Now, earlier in your testimony you mentioned some other properties that you had, the general store, Ideal or Ideal, held in the name of your niece Nermina. Have you been able to recover that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to actually take legal steps in order to do so or was that a fairly simple matter?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a simple matter. They called me after ten years and they returned my entire property in Bosanski Samac, but, however, everything has been stolen and destroyed, so I can't live in there any more. I would need a lot of money, some 50.000 or 60.000 German marks to improve the condition of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The property that was in the shop, in the general store, is that all gone?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next the pharmacy, which was held in Enver's name. Have you been able to recover that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but everything was taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the video rental shop? Have you been able to recover that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was all recovered, together with the shop. However, the interior has been emptied: The video cassettes, the VCRs and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the cafe Sedrvan?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sedrvan cafe has been completely destroyed to the ground, and everything in it was taken away. And then later on they blew it up. So all that remains are tiles and a part of the fence. Everything else was blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever received any compensation for the destruction of your cafe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't received anything from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any rents for use of those properties that I've asked you about, the shops and the cafe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. How can anyone pay me anything when everything has been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it -- when -- when talking about Sedrvan cafe, the witness said that -- well, it is page 5, lines 1 to 4, only one addition. We heard that he said that his neighbours told him that, and we don't see this in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At what stage? At the end of the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you can clear that with the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. But I'm just not sure which answer. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Page 5, lines 1 to 4. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you've been told the cafe, Sedrvan, has been destroyed, that is, you've been informed of that fact by people, or have you been there and actually seen the remains of it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it. I was in Samac to recover my property, and I saw that it had been destroyed completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you if whilst you were in custody you ever received any information, notification, any official notification of what it was that you had done to bring about your incarceration, and you said you were never told. Following your release, has anyone ever told you why it was that you were locked up for well over two years? And when I say "told you," I mean in some sort of official capacity.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was obvious. I was locked up because I was a Muslim. This is why they took me to the camp, not just me, but all of my fellow citizens, Muslims and Croats. All of us were taken away the Sava River. We were exchanged in Dragalici and elsewhere. We went to the camps. People -- other people were deported. There is information to support that. I was incarcerated for exactly two years and six months, and part of it was unregistered. When I came to Batkovici, I was registered there. So that's some two and a half years in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that answer perfectly well, and I have no quarrel with that evidence at all. But what I'm actually asking is: Has anyone given you an official explanation? Has the government of the Republika Srpska or the police in Bosanski Samac ever said to you or given you a document following your release: "Look, this is the reason why you were locked up: Insurrection, treason genocide," something like that, anything at all?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In all of the places in Samac -- you're asking me about Samac. I have brothers there. Two have died. I was arrested because I was wealthy. They mostly arrested wealthy people and beat them so that as to prevent them from ever coming back and in order to eradicate any trace of them, so that they would teach you not to ever go back to Samac, and Samac is my native town. This is where I was born. That's all. It is very difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And one last question: Prior to all of these events, prior to the 16th of April and the 17th of April and everything that followed, up until that point of time, had you had any plans or desire to leave your town and the place where you were born and had lived all your life?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that nobody on this planet would leave his or her native town, regardless of which country they live in. People tend to go back to their native towns. I lived in America for two and a half years. I was South Dakota champion in chess. I played in a government tournament and I was a champion there, and I was well taken care of there. But still, I felt this need to go back to my native town, Samac. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the end of the examination-in-chief? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, my learned friends. Cross-examined by Mr. Vukovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bobic. My name is Srdjan Vukovic. I am Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic, and I will be conducting cross-examination. I presume that the Prosecutor has explained to you what it will look like. It will approximately look the same as the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not told anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is a small difference. You and I speak the same language, and I would kindly ask you to make a small break after my question so that we can give interpreters a chance to translate my question and your answer. Mr. Bobic, yesterday you stated to the Prosecutor that you joined the SDA -- please wait for me to ask the question and then answer it. So that you joined the SDA when the parties were established. Is that right? You also stated before this Trial Chamber that you joined the SDA in 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, as far as I remember, political parties were founded and, and multi-party elections were held in 1990.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was officially after the elections, once all the data was verified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please tell us: Did you become a member in 1990 or was it in 1991?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be either way. I don't remember the exact date. It is possible. But just to make it clear, I have been a member of the SDA from the very beginning, and I can't tell you now exactly when it was founded. All of the political parties were founded approximately in the same time period, and I have been a member of that party -- of that party's board from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated yesterday before this Trial Chamber that in the SDA you were a member of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Executive board?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were seven of us when we established the board. It was in the very beginning. That's correct. There's no doubt about that. All of it was legal. The party itself was legally established. It was a democratic party, which is further indicated by its name. It was called the party of democratic action, SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, please avoid repeating examination-in-chief, because all of these questions, the evidence was given yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, please tell us: What does the word "action" stand for?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does the "action" stand for? You should know that yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, counsel is asking questions on behalf of the Trial Chamber, so please answer the questions. If you don't know, you say so.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Party of Democratic Action stands for the beginning of -- "action" stands for the beginning of acting, "party" stands for political party, and "democratic" stands for democratic. It was similar for other parties, the SDS, with the HDZ, and there was also a party called Croatian Democratic Movement, and the SDS stood for Serbian Democratic Party, and there were also reformist parties, with Mr. Kecmanovic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please control the flow of evidence. We don't need all these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, please tell us: What activities did you perform as member of the executive board of the SDA within your party?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my activities? Well, we went to the mosque. We wanted to look into establishing our organisations in town, because people started segregating the Serbs, the Croats. They looked as -- it looked as though we were together, but we were not. We had no minorities in Samac. The Muslims were a majority, and we had our party platform, just like any other party. Our platform did not include attacking somebody or entering into arguments with anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I have to interrupt you. Can you please tell me what specific activities you carried out?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you have in mind when you say "activities." It was a Muslim party called the SDA. It was the party of Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. What I have in mind is your personal activities, as members of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had no specific activities. What do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were seven of you in the executive board?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who else was there in the board?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Hakija Bobacic, Izet Izetbegovic. He was a relative of Alija Izetbegovic, the president. Then myself, then Husein Ceribasic, Aziz Pasic, and Abdulah Imsirovic. He was effendi and after the elections Sulejman Tihic joined the party and became the chairman of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, can you tell me who was on the executive board in 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. In 1992, Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the chairman, the president of the party, but can you tell me who were the members of the executive board in 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was Hakija Babacic. I was never in the top leadership. I was simply a member and a member of the board. They came to my place to eat there, since I had a shop, a cafe. They would come to Sedrvan to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, in your statement given to the Prosecutor in June of this year, on page 2, in paragraph 5, you stated that as member of the executive board, you assisted in fund-raising for the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There's nothing contentious. But we could, clarify what funds you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I would like you to explain that.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Well, I assisted financially. They would also come to my place to eat, delegations of the SDA from Sarajevo. It was all in the process of being established, just like in any other party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go back to one issue that you did not fully explain. You didn't tell us who else was the member of the executive board of the SDA in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you want to hear the members?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to hear who the members were. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember all that. You probably have the list. I can't remember that now. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: -- objecting to the question, but we've already had twice now two separate questions relating to the executive board. I don't see the point in listing it for a third time. Perhaps the witness can be asked to provide names of any additional members of those who might have been there in 1992, otherwise we'll have the list again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are going round and round, Mr. Vukovic. You can put questions to him was it so-and-so, whatever name you think was in the executive board and let the witness answer, because we're taking too long on the membership of the SDA board.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. However, the witness gave us the names of the executive board members in 1990, so he can remember that well, based on which, I believe, that he should also be able to tell us who were the members in 1992. It is obvious that the witness is avoiding answering that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not. I told you everything I know. There's no problem there. The membership frequently changed, in every party: In HDZ, in the SDS, and so on. Sulejman Tihic was not on the board when I was there. He came there because we needed a lawyer who could lead the party and he accepted that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I didn't ask you about Mr. Tihic. He was the chairman of the party in 1992. I asked you about members of the executive board in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was before [Indiscernible] who then he replaced Izet Izetbegovic. You know that. If you want to know more --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm asking you for the last time who were members of the executive board in 1992. I'm not asking about presidents; I'm asking about members, apart from you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hakija Babacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the executive board had only two members?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The executive board had more people, you are asking me who was in the leadership, so will you please clarify the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll move on to another topic. THE COURT: Do you have names of the members of the board, which you should confront the witness with?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I will do that a little later. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It doesn't help us at all when you look at the indictment, because if there are any activities that you wanted to allege, you better put the matters directly to the witness. You know the allegations against your client, and one would hope that you would spend time dealing with cross-examination which will help his defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, at the meetings of your party, did you talk about procuring weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not, because --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bobic, on page 3 of your statement of June this year, you said the following, paragraph 8: "There was -- there had been some discussion in the SDA as to whether we should try to get arms. Because of the war in Croatia and the activities of the JNA."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody said that in the party. But yes, there was talk. However, you can't take a rifle to attack a tank or somebody who hits you from above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I asked was whether the party discussed whether you should get weapons for your party.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No -- yes, there was some talk, but not that we personally should procure weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were the arms obtained?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the party and the colleagues know it -- I mean the accused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, will you please try to only answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, do you know Mr. Hakija Babacic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. Professor. He was the manager of the food-processing factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us: What is his ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't ask me such stupid questions, please. You know that Hakija is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, just answer the questions put to you by counsel. If the questions are not supposed to be put to you, the Prosecution will object or the Trial Chamber will give instructions to counsel. Don't be rude to counsel. You are in a court. Just answer the questions. If you don't know the answers, say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I'm asking you that for a very simple reason, that members of the Chamber are people who are not our nationals, either of your country or mine, and they do not know that. I'm asking you that merely so that we can inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I know what the ethnic origin of Mr. Hakija is. What we are doing here is for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to explain it to me, and no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us: What did Mr. Hakija do in the executive board?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the vice-president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Midhat Somtic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Contic. Yes, I know him, but he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were his duties in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was simply on the board, didn't have any special duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, we received information from the top leadership of your party that you, together with Mr. Babacic and Mr. Contic, were the chief advocates of the armament of Muslims and members of the SDA; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. When the armament started, I left the board. You should know that. That is the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Vukovic. The interpreters didn't catch, neither did I hear, the translation when you said that Mr. Bobic, along with the other two gentlemen, were the chief -- and then we have a blank of the blank of the SDA; is that true? That's line 2 of page 16. What were you actually asking him? Were the chief what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain it right away, Your Honour. I asked Mr. Bobic -- I told Mr. Bobic that we had information from the ground, from the topmost leadership of the SDA party, that this witness, together with Mr. Babacic and Mr. Contic, were the principal advocates of the armament of Muslims in the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, tell us: Was Hakija Babacic a national of the B and H?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hakija Babacic is a Yugoslav. I think he's a Yugoslav. He comes from Kruskovo Polje, from Montenegro or something. But he was involved for a long time -- now, I don't know how long, but he spent many years in Samac. He has lived in Samac for a long time. He lived in Samac for 10, 15 years in the former Yugoslavia. Of course, I don't know when everybody came to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps come from Sandzak, that is, the south of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's not from Sandzak, but I cannot recall where he came from. I think he said he was from Vitromirica, if there is a place like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Mr. Bobic, did the SDA set up its Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, because I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My only question is whether it formed this Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not while I was in it. I know there was Territorial Defence in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Serbs, Muslims, and Croats there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left it, was the Crisis Staff established then?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the -- did the SDA draw up its wartime plan?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either. Perhaps it did, but I wasn't there, so I cannot say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we generally agree that the SDA set up certain sections, such as, for instance, supply service, monitoring service, observation service?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not whilst I was there. There were people who helped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Tell us: What did they help with?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I helped the party, that I donated funds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I mean you said assistance, and I asked you what you meant by this.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody help with obtaining weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you should also pause and allow the witness to answer, so that we don't have a problem with the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, as far as I could gather from your testimony, you remained on the board as its member -- just wait until I finish my question -- but later -- at the later stage, that is, prior to the 17th of April, you did not actively participate in the work of the party.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you went on living in Samac and working there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And people continued to patronise your restaurant?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of all ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, you are aware, being a member of the SDA, that Alija Fitozovic and Izet Izetbegovic obtained a considerable quantity of explosives and weapons for members of your party, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that I quit the board, that I was not active, and now you are contradicting yourself. So let's try and help these people here. I didn't know -- I wasn't aware of that, nor did I know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, Mr. Bobic, in your statement that you gave to the Tribunal in June this year, you said the following, passage 8: "I heard that Alija Fitozovic allegedly bought weapons in Croatia."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I did say that, perhaps I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There are two counsels from the Prosecution, which shows that it's a strong objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I'm here just for the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason we both jumped up is because I was waiting to see if counsel would read out the whole sentence, and I jumped up because I was, of course, the person who took the statement in 2002, and I had put a question to the witness and this is how he answered me. I specifically elicited this information. And the full statement is not what's on the record. It is: "I heard that Alija Fitozovic may have bought weapons in Croatia, but I know nothing about it." And that's what he said. And I think if that's put on the record, the Bench will understand this man's testimony here today is the same as it was in June. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, is that the correct quotation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, you said that you had heard that Alija Fitozovic may have bought weapons. So tell us: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those could have been rumours around in Samac. These here are arming themselves or those over there are arming themselves, but this is all unofficial. That is what I said in the statement. I'm telling you that I was no longer holding any duties because I was preparing a new shop before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. You've explained it to us already. There is no need to go into that again. However, you told us, and you stated that too, you continued living and working in Samac, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you are repeating yourself. I'm wondering whether you have any cross-examination which touches the defence of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Avoid repeating yourself, avoid the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour, but the witness is evading answering certain questions, and I thus have to take the witness into this matter, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not the view of the Trial Chamber. The witness is answering. When he doesn't know, he says so. He left the party. He doesn't know what was going on. And that's it. He's not evading. He's giving answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour, but I'm asking the witness about events in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, did the SDA put up barricades in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not. Those were barricades which were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. My only question was whether the SDA put up any barricades.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the Territorial Defence which put them up, and you all know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the SDA organise patrols in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I told the Court that my son had been killed, and I stopped being active at the time, and I do not know what went on at that time, so don't make me lie here. I cannot lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness not speak over each other.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot lie about what I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, did you see any armed patrols in the town? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see them. I don't know if somebody else did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, can we agree about a certain fact --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that in the period of time preceding the hostilities, a few months before that, the arming of citizens, of inhabitants of Samac began, namely, Muslims and Croats and Serbs alike?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it a moment ago: We had a multi-ethnic Territorial Defence, and that is true. There were Serbs and Muslims and Croats together as the defence of the town. Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, will you please listen to what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about citizens of Samac, not about the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not. Again, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, in your statement that you gave to the Tribunal in June 2002, on page 3 and page 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you mean the statement the witness gave to the Prosecution ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's important to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 10, you explain how, unfortunately, that tragic event took place in the Valentino coffee bar, and after that you say: "I believe that that incident brought about intensified armament of the population because people felt under attack." Did you say that or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably happened then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my son was killed on the 14th of February, in Valentino, for unknown reasons, there were all the indicia, that he had brought the grenade to the coffee bar --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. I don't want to ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness and the counsel are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, we're having problems with the interpreters because you are speaking over each other. And I think the question to your answer was given, yes, in line 12, page 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I meant only because the interpreters had said that it was not in, and I merely wanted to have it repeated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, can we agree that at that time in Samac high tension reigned between ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you if you can come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on now to events immediately after the beginning of the hostilities. Two or three days after April 17th, you and your family moved over to your neighbours', Nogic's?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us: That day when you moved over to your neighbour, to Nogic's, was Samac shelled?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shells were falling. I don't know where they came from. But yes, shells were hitting certain areas. That was why we took shelter at Nogic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Samac was shelled? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, it wasn't all that bad, but there were shells falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I'd like to ask you to explain to the Chamber: How far is your house from the bank of the Sava, roughly?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the other side of the bridge over the Sava River --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One kilometre, as the crow flies. I mean --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I haven't finished my question. Will you please wait? From the other bank, across the bridge over the Sava, is the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Slavonski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please explain to the Chamber: How far is your house from the Bosna River?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never measured it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five hundred, six hundred metres, thereabouts, perhaps a little -- give or take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other side is --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I was about to ask you that. From the direction of Slavonski Samac and Prud, was the artillery firing at Samac from that direction?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you for sure. I don't know. Perhaps it did, perhaps it didn't. There were all kinds of rumours. It probably did. It is more likely, at least I believe so, that it did, because it was on both sides. Serbs and Croats fired at Bosnia, because -- at least that's what I heard, because some houses were destroyed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, two or three days later, after the shelling, was there electricity and water supply in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had water supply, but electricity would go off occasionally, and then the same would apply to water. And Muslims, and I myself, did not have electricity. I don't know about Serb houses. But I also know that we had no telephone lines, no communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I asked you was water and electricity.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, occasionally. Sometimes we would have an outage and sometimes we would have regular supply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can we agree that water and electricity were not supplied to all of the citizens?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to all. But I have to say that we did not have telephone lines and we did not have electrical power. There were occasional outages due to shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, but despite that, the population had regular supply of bread and milk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, yesterday you stated before this Trial Chamber that you learned that you had to wear white armbands upon leaving your house?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when we went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You even told us what they looked like?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you please explain to the Trial Chamber: Who did you learn this from?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was announced on the radio that Samac was a Serb town, that people leaving houses should have white armbands and they should not move about in groups. There was a lady announcer. It was a female voice that announced it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, who at the time was the editor of the radio station?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Samac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Novak Tenasije, and Stevan Stevic was the president of the memorial hall, as far as I know. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bobic, you were taken, upon your arrest, to the SUP building on the 23rd of May. That's what you told us. Can you tell us: Why were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already replied to that. MR. DI FAZIO: [Previous translation continues] ... on about four --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: The witness is right. He has replied to it on about four or five occasions. Never given a reason, not in the MUP, not in the TO, not in Batkovici, nor ever since, as to the reason he spent two years in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If counsel has got reasons, it's better to put them directly to the witness, if counsel's instructions are that reasons were given to the witness, then it's better to put it directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, you gave a statement to a secret agency for investigation and documentation?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was on the 12th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What agency do you have in mind? I didn't give a statement to any agency. Your question is not clear to me. And what date it was? I apologise. I misheard the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the Muslim agency which is known under the acronym AID; it's, in fact, secret police.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never gave such a statement. Give me the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never given such a statement, never. That's invented. That's illegal. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, this statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Vukovic. Of course, I well understand what AID is and where it's located, but for the sake of the record, I don't think it's very clear to say: "You gave a statement to the Muslim agency." It could be a Muslim agency in any country in the world where there are Muslims. Can you just be specific, for clarity's sake? MR. DI FAZIO: If I may also pick up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazios. MR. DI FAZIO: If I may also pick up from what follows from Your Honour's proposition put to Mr. Vukovic. It also end with the assertion that it's the secret police, and I think that if that's going to be put to the witness -- sorry, if that comment is going to be made, it should put fairly and squarely to the witness so he can say, "Oh, yes, it's cloak and dagger stuff. They are the secret police." Or he can say: No, that's complete nonsense" as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vukovic. Please clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document, or rather, the statement, which the witness gave to the agency for investigation and documentation, sectors AID, in Tuzla, on the 12th of March, 1998, has been filed with this Tribunal by the Prosecution, ERN number 00602426. I would like the usher to assist me to put this statement to the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Can I see the document, please? I wonder if Defence counsel can tell us the ERN number of the English translation, and if they have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have not received the English translation, and therefore I don't have the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So this document is only in Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only in B/C/S version, because we didn't receive from the Prosecution, the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but if you knew that you are going to use it in your cross-examination, why didn't you have it translated in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Because the [Interpretation] Because the Prosecution has the English version. I wasn't about to read from the statement. All I wanted was to ask the witness whether he had signed the statement. MR. DI FAZIO: That would be objected to because it would be pointless. There's no point in asking him whether he signs a piece of paper unless there's something in the piece of paper that's of use to the Defence or to the Prosecution. But I certainly don't have the English version. I'm not even aware of the existence of this document. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence prepared their cross-examination. They knew that they were going to use this document. If that is their intention, they should have made sure that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. May I clarify this very simple issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, clarify it, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We don't need into all these details. During the preparation of the cross-examination of this witness, the Defence, of course, was in possession of the Prosecution document. It was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Although it was not in English. It's not a big thing. Our opinion was that it is not in dispute that the Prosecution will check everything with regard to this witness. Now we think that our learned friends are a little bit surprised. So the bottom line, Your Honour, is: It is not a question of the content of this statement. No. It is not part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then what is the point of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The point is one fact, one event, which arises from various sources, including this document. And now this witness denying, which is absolutely surprising for the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And he simply should say whether you signed it or not, simple as that, and then we shall proceed with other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, then, can we have the passage, the relevant passage, read slowly so that we have it on record, translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. But I would kindly suggest, Your Honour, first of all to clarify whether this witness signed this document or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then we shall go with this passage. Absolutely, I agree. Thank you very much for your attention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, have you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never signed this statement. There are thousands of my signatures in Bosanski Samac, in the revenue office, in courts, and so on. I think that this document here had been falsified. This is a forgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to put the document on the ELMO so that the accused and the Trial Chamber can see it. I would like to ask the usher to focus on the signature. The signature can be found at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, this statement was given to the Agency for Investigation and Documentation -- Mr. Bobic, please let me finish -- sector AID, in Tuzla, and has been registered under number 5/8-02-260 [sic], on the 6th of March, 1998. I apologise, but there's been a mistake in the transcript. It's not 260; it's 620. Mr. Bobic, please take a look at every page and tell me whether this is your signature. Is your signature on each page?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A signature can be falsified. This can be a forgery. There are thousands of my signatures in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, the question is simple. Check every page. Is that your signature? And then answer. So you don't have to say anything else; you simply answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, on page 4, ERN number 602429, there is your signature and your ID number issued by the public Security Service in Brcko. Is that your ID card number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would ask the usher to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this number 0060 -- and so on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I mean page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be put on the ELMO, please, the fourth page of this document, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What ID card number did you say? I can't see it here. The number that I have here is 0 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, Mr. Bobic, is whether, in 1998, you had an ID card number 5508/97, and was it issued by the public security service in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue date that I have is 18th of December, 1997, and my card was issued in Brcko. Here, you can take a look at it. This is the date here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, can you please read out the number of your ID card?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number is -- do you mean the date of issue or the registration number? Which number do you mean? 19 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we get through this much faster than we are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has produced an ID card --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but refused to read the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He hasn't refused. Yes. All I want to know: Mr. Bobic, the card you are holding, is that your identification card?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When did you get it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no interpretation. We didn't get interpretation in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, please be so kind -- please put your ELMO -- put your ID card on the ELMO, and please read out the registration number of your ID card.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read it out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please be so kind and read out to us the number that we can see on page 4 of your statement? MR. DI FAZIO: We can see it's the same number. What's the point of the question? I mean, 5508/97. What's the point of getting the witness to read out what's obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The counsel just wants to make sure that it's the same number. Yes, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, are you still maintaining that the signatures on all four pages of this statement are not yours, in fact? This was in 1998, in Tuzla, is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That was the statement on genocide, genocide against Muslims in Tuzla. It was conducted by Rifat Karic and this had to do with the genocide in Srebrenica. When I came back from America, they located me in Tuzla and they interviewed me about the genocide in Srebrenica, in Bosanski Samac, and generally in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They interviewed me about that, because I spent a lot of time in the camp. That's why. It wasn't clear to me. Because this refers to genocide. It has nothing to do with politics, as you are implying. Or at least maybe you're not implying, but that's how had I saw it. I have proven that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, please take this statement and read out the heading explaining to whom you gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave it to Rifat Karic. I know that a hundred per cent. This is a man who works on genocide issues. I know what I have signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, please put page 1 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please assist us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, on page 1 of the statement, which has the ERN number 00602426, in the last paragraph of your statement, you said this: "Then Stevo Todorovic told me that I am the greatest culprit for the fact that the war broke out in Bosanski Samac. After that, Todorovic beat me with a baton and kicked me in my chest and so on." Mr. Bobic, did you state this? Please, just a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that. I did state that Stevan Todorovic kicked me and beat me in the chest. And why don't you read what is stated up there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, this is just a passage out of this statement which was read to you by counsel, and he asked you: "Did you state that?" The answer should be yes or no. Do not argue with counsel. Simply answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours. Perhaps it would be better if the witness himself read out this passage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, the judge asked you, and we are expecting you to give us a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer was not clear. It could be yes or it could be no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters are saying that the witness's answer was not clear. It could be yes, it could be no. Can you repeat your answer, Mr. Bobic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will. The first reply to that first sentence, where Stiv said that I was to blame for the war in Bosanski Samac and that he beat me in my chest and kicked me, and now he's asking me to say yes or no. And then that would also imply an answer to this other bit, that he didn't beat me. But to the other part, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you state this or not? Give us a simple answer.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is an ambiguous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bobic, on page 2 of that same statement, with the ERN number 00602427, in paragraph 2, you stated: "On the 25th of May, 1992, I was once again summoned for an interview, but on that occasion I was interrogated by Simo Bozic, a lawyer, misdemeanour judge in Bosanski Samac. This interrogation was conducted in the same office where I was taken on the first occasion for an interview with Stevan Todorovic. Bozic told me that I was accused for being a main supplier for the SDA in Bosanski Samac and that due to that, I had to remain in prison, in the building of the public security service." Did you state this? Just briefly, yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Generally, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we perhaps make a break now and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we could proceed after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue at 1100 hours. I just want to know how much Mr. Vukovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall continue at 1100 hours

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, we don't have much time, and I will ask you only a few short questions and then we shall be over with this part of the cross-examination. Please, will you answer my question briefly and clearly. Did you, on the 12th of March, 1998, on the official premises in Brcko, give to authorised officials of AID sector Tuzla, give any statement and sign it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, on 3rd of April, 1998, you gave a statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, are you through with that --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Other statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it marked for identification only, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's ERN -- no. This one. MR. DI FAZIO: Just while we're on that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- topic, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I believe the document that's marked for identification is dated the 16th of March. Mr. Vukovic put to the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: not sure. Is he talking about this statement or is he aware of statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. The statement the witness was discussing before break, what is the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that my learned friend wasn't -- didn't look at the statement properly. In the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you are the one who introduced --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seventh line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- [Previous translation continues] ... -- I just want to know what is the document dated and what is the title? MR. DI FAZIO: Fine. I've got something that says 16th of April -- 16th of March, 1998, and then I can see the 12th of March in the body of the preamble. All I want to know is this: Is that question that my learned friend asked of the witness, he was referring to this statement in -- that's been marked for identification? And I think Mr. Vukovic can confirm that. We're only talking about the one statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is one statement, which was filed on the 16th of March, 1998, but the witness gave the statement on the 12th of March, 1998. And the number under which the statement was filed in the AID, sector Tuzla, is 5-8/02-620, and the ERN number is 00602426 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the number, please, for identification purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D49/1 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. You can proceed, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, to the Tribunal, that is, to the Prosecutor of the Tribunal, you gave a statement on the 3rd of April, 1998. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I gave something to the Tribunal. Commissions came. I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the Tribunal on the 3rd of April, 1998, on page with the ERN number 00637124 in B/C/S, and in English it has the ERN number 602439 -- on that page, you explain how you were exchanged on the 6th of October, 1994 and that at the same time some other people were also exchanged. I will read out the names that you gave. Was Kemal Mehinovic exchanged at the same time with you?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nesib Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mahmud Arapovic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namik Arapovic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hasan Ceribasic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mujo Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, and brother Slavko -- Salko. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirsad Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fuad Skenderovic.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sead Mahic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Muris Mahic?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, are you aware if any of these individuals who were exchanged at the same time as you were gave their statements to the agency for investigation and documentation, short, AID, sector Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. Mujo lives in America. I don't know, really. I have no contact with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only a short question: At the time when you gave your statement, was any of them there to give his statement at the same time? And that is my last question.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: We gave our statements after we were exchanged in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All together?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. In Sarajevo, after the exchange, we gave statements at the SUP, and perhaps there is some confusion about that, because all of us who were exchanged from Samac, we gave statements then, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bobic. I'm Novak Lukic, and I will now ask you questions on behalf of the accused Miroslav Tadic. I will tell you straight away that my questions will have to do with two or three subjects only, and I will not go into any of your disagreeable memories, even though all of it must be of that nature. Could we look at the map that we've already used in this Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want the witness to look at that map. But we need an unmarked, a clean copy of that document, D27/3, which we have already used. And when the witness says that he can find his bearing there, this is the map of the town of Bosanski Samac. I will then ask him to mark three places, that is, his house, the house that he found shelter at Nogic's, and the place where his coffee bar -- where his restaurant was. So I want the usher to show this map to the Prosecutor so that they can see that the map is unmarked, and then we shall ask the witness to see if he can find his way around the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And please, can you ask him to mark with numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the map, Mr. Bobic. We've already used this map in these proceedings. Perhaps it would be better if you take and put it in front of you, and then we'll put it on the ELMO later on. So what I'd like to know, and I will ask you to mark it, if you can identify the location of your house. You told us that it was on Lola Ribar Street. Where was the house that belonged to Nogics, where you took shelter in the early days of the war, and where was your restaurant? If you can do that, then --

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Just a moment. You know what? I apologise, but I can't really get my bearings here, because the streets have been changed, and these are only squares. So I show Marsala Tito here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO and take the pointer? And if you can't find your way around it, I won't insist on it, if you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Perhaps you go to my house like, this from the police, then you take the first street to the left, not the one towards the memorial building but somewhere here, and then you -- and there is a crossroads. I've already explained that. A big one. Which takes you over -- I've forgotten the streets, I know the first one was called Marsala Tito, the second was Ivo Lola Ribar, the third was Pere Bosica, I think, then Vuk Karadzic. I don't know. But as you come out, then you head in my direction, and my neighbour Vlajko and his brother Miro -- there is this crossroads, and my house is straight behind here. This -- my -- is the second one, if that is correct here. Then my house should be here. So you don't -- you don't head for the memorial centre, but you go to SUP and then the first street and then the first to the left is Nogic's house and my house is right next to it, and there is this crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need to identify it any more, because obviously the witness says he cannot really find his way around it, but if we can ask him to explain it, I think it will be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. There's no use using the map which the witness cannot read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is what I'd like to know, Mr. Bobic: You said that you took shelter in Mr. Nogic's house. Yesterday you mentioned Mesud Nogic. Was that the house, Mesud Nogic's where you found shelter or Idriz Nogic's?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Idriz's house, because Dr. Mesud Nogic built another house, and the former was my neighbour. So this was the joint house. But then he built his other house and moved over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is what I wanted to clear up. So this is Idriz Nogic's house that you went to, the old house?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave a statement, you already told us, Mr. Vukovic showed you, in 1998. You gave the statement to the OTP. And I noticed that this statement -- I must say, I was impressed by the large number of names and other information that at that time you gave to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So the witness doesn't get confused because I can foresee here getting into a problem. Mr. Lukic has said -- Mr. Vukovic showed you -- Mr. Vukovic did not show the witness any statement apart from the one that says it was taken by the AID Tuzla. So I don't want the witness to think that that witness -- that document that he was shown is the one that now Mr. Lukic is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... -- that he referred to it but he didn't show it to the witness, so please do lead the witness correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm sorry. Yes. Mr. Vukovic merely mentioned that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But now I will only briefly address this statement which you gave to the OTP on the 3rd of April, 1998 and which you signed. I said that I noticed that you mentioned quite a number of names in the text. Mr. Vukovic has read out to you the names, and you told that those were the people who were exchanged at the same time as you were. However, in this statement I did not see you mention anywhere Cvijetin Stevanovic -- Stjepanovic [As interpreted]. Do you remember, you speak about this incident, how he came to you in Batkovici and about the document that you signed. Did you then speak to the representatives of the OTP at that time?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: There was no need for me to speak about that, because I could not enter the so-called Serb Republic, so that I had no contact, and I believe it is clear. As soon as I established a contact, then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this Cvijetin Stevanovic from before he came to Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No. He lived in Loncari, in Samac, Loncari, quite far from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 83 of the transcript, you said that when he came, you said: "I know this man."

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
