utterances.text: Everybody knew me, everybody who lived there knew me, because I had my shop and music and people knew me in Modrica, in Odzak, and other places. People used to come to my restaurant for dinner, so that everybody knew me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that there was a lady lawyer with him. I'd like to know if your wife also came with them, Ediba. Was she there?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Not the first time, no, I can't remember. She did come with him once. I'll find it for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the witness looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday the witness said to my learned friend that he had another document in addition to the other one, and I merely wanted to see what is this other document and wanted to see if that is the document that the Prosecutor has disclosed to us or whether it is some other document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He mentioned it yesterday to the Prosecutor, but he said -- he mentioned a document, and I simply do not know whether it is a different document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the witness said anything, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think if you looked look at the record, the witness explained he brought the original of the document that was tendered, I think it's P135 into evidence. He had the original here and he explained that to the Chamber. He then said he also had a -- there was another document which existed which related --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. I'm sorry. The witness then said he had another document which related to his sister's property, that it was also taken away, but the witness made clear that he had the original of P136 with him and that's what he went to get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's get on, then. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need the original, because we accepted this document P136 [as interpreted]. My question concerned your wife, and we'll come back to the comment later. But you said on that occasion when he came with this lady lawyer that your wife wasn't there, on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I can't really remember. She came once. She came once, but I can't remember whether it was with him. You know, I was in the camp. I was all lost. I do remember that she came once. She went to Bijeljina, Goran Blagojevic, I think it's his name, and he gave her the authorisation in writing to visit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is very simple. If you don't remember, say so. Do you remember if, when she came to visit you in Batkovici, was that before you signed the document for this Cvijetin or after that? If you do not remember, I won't insist on it.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I can't remember. After all, it was 11 years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what my learned friend has said and what you said, you said that you had a document with you which had to do with your wife's sister, Amira, and I also suppose it has to do with this Cvijetin Stevanovic. Now, if you have this document, I'd like to see it.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Here you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it will be better if you put it on the ELMO. Now, could we have the upper part of the document, please? Could we -- could we simply -- so that we can see what this is about. And now if you can move it up a little bit so that we can see the signatures.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: You see here he forced all -- he forced women to sign this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it wouldn't be bad if the Prosecution could supply us with a copy of this document. All I can do is confirm that it is the same power of attorney issued to the name of Mr. Kemal Bobic except that here it also covers his sister-in-law and his -- and her two daughters and it is of the same date, the 6th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, the same day when I write it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose it was the matter of joint property?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now can we see the stamp? Can we see the other side, please, the other side of the document? Could you read out to us -- what does this round seal say?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: "Republika Srpska, basic court in Brcko, Brcko."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: The date is the same. 10th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that it is the 6th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Brcko, 6th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is the same power of attorney, say like the one that you wrote -- that you signed for Cvijetin except that it was signed by these ladies?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. It was in Samac, and then he came to Brcko with me with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps have a copy of this power of attorney with you where Amira -- which Amira gave him for this property?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I don't. I just happened to bring this along. What I have is the judgement of the Court in Brcko, because I won that case. Here. I have it all. May I have a look?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Does the Court allow that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I want to know is: What is the point of all this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I put a question yesterday to Mrs. Bobic, and now I just learned that there is another document. I wish to establish: How was, in fact, that property transferred? All I received from the Prosecutor is the power of attorney, in his name. I'm not going to put any questions to the witness, but I would like to ask the Prosecutor to take over these documents from the witness so that we can carry out certain verfications through our investigators.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That has already been done because there was another judgement passed down in Brcko and he had lost the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Prosecution dealt with the documents that mattered with their case. So if you want to conduct investigations which have nothing to do with this case, then you have to do that on your own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I wanted to acquire information from the witness so that I can carry out my investigation. All I want to know: What was the registration number of that case in Samac? If the witness can tell me that, then I can carry my investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it can be quite easily done. All you have to do is go to the Court in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In which case, then there is no point in this other power of attorney which was signed by the ladies. There is no point in referring to it, because the power of attorney which the witness dealt with regarding his property has been -- is on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to go into these civil law issues, but this was a joint property relationship between this witness and the family of his late brother, and forceful confiscation or forceful takeover of his property from Cvijetin Stevanovic ^Stepanovic, and this is why I needed the information regarding his sister-in-law, Amira. This is all one and the same case. I think that they altogether were litigants in this one case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. All I want to do is to instruct the usher to get photocopies of the other power of attorney regarding the other property, so that the registry has a copy, and then we can mark it for identification only. Yes, you can proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wish to correct the transcript. The registry just told me that I referred to this document as P136, this power of attorney, when in fact it was document P135 it was it was issued by this witness, Bobic Kemal, to Cvijetin Stjepanovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one more question. You have just confirmed me that you co-owned all of your property together with your sister-in-law, Amira, who was the wife of your late brother and the sister of your wife; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I gathered it, she and her family lived in another part of your duplex, which was the house with two parts to it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. It was one large house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, do you remember that you and Amira signed a gift contract gifting away part of your house to Gordana Pavlovic, who was the girlfriend of your late son, and that took place sometime in the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: All of them, many of them came to the camp to have documents signed. What else could I do? I was locked up in the camp and they could do as they pleased. They had to fight over getting my signature. They knew what kind of a house I had. I had a large house with four three-room apartments. Everybody wanted to loot my property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just put a very clear question to you.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. Gordana came with her father, Dusko Pavlovic, and her brother, Branko. They came to visit me in Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that answer complete? Because it doesn't answer the part of signing a gift contract. The answer is simply that they came to visit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He didn't reply to me fully, but now the witness just confirmed to me that Gordana came with her father and brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you remember signing the deed gifting away part of your property to her? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't remember that, because this is what they told me: That the Municipal Assembly would not let them enter the house until I and my family signed the document, because we were supposed to be expelled. How can you give away your own house? I think that's ridiculous. I don't need to comment on this any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When disclosing certain documents to us, the Prosecutor also gave us a sheet of paper which is barely legible. It has an ERN number 00604078. I would kindly ask you to take a look at this sheet of paper. I tried to decipher it, but I was unable, and I would like to ask you now whether you have any recollection regarding this document. I have a sufficient number of copies for the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have translation in English, because I was unable to read the B/C/S version of this document as I have received it from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you, sir, have any knowledge regarding this, could this perhaps pertain to Gordana Pavlovic? Do you see a signature on this document? Do you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I never signed this. I can't even tell what it says here. Bobic Kemal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is this signature down there perhaps yours? There's a number 1 and then a signature next to it. Does that look like your signature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is totally illegible. You yourself said you couldn't decipher it at all, so how do you expect the witness ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I wanted to ask the witness about this and see whether he had signed anything of this kind and whether he could assist us with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is completely illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, do you remember giving this document to the Prosecution? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, not this document, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I will have to carry out further consultations with the Prosecution to see where they acquired this document.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't know whether my wife perhaps submitted this. I have all of the originals here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness doesn't know. He has given us the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we introduce this document as an ID document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I oppose to this document being tendered, because it is quite unclear, and there are a lot of things here that are rigged. I am here interrogated as an accused, not as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, you leave that to the Prosecution and the Defence. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I oppose to the document being tendered as well, if Your Honours please. There's simply no evidenced establishing what it is. It's meaningless. Illegible so far and, at the most, it could be given an ID number. For what it's worth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. For what it's worth, we shall have it marked for identification only. MR. DI FAZIO: The Prosecution's submission essentially is there is no coherent evidence about the piece of paper at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Can we have it marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The previous document, the power of attorney dated 6th of October, 1993, shall be marked D73/3 ter ID. This document shall be marked D74/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, we will now change topics entirely, and please don't think that I wish to accuse you of anything. All I wanted was to clarify certain things regarding this sheet of paper that was furnished to me by the Prosecution. Now we will turn to an entirely different topic concerning the exchange and the information you had about the exchanges while you were in Batkovici. You told us that Batkovici looked like a typical camp. The warden that you mentioned, and the warden of that prisoner, was he somebody from the military?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I know that he was a taxman in Bijeljina, and then during the war he was promoted to the rank of major, and all of us addressed him as "major." I learned how to address officers when I was in the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this camp, or the collections centre, as they called it, and its functioning and organisation was under the jurisdiction of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a typical camp. We were transferred from Samac to Batkovici, so that was one coherent group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is whether you know that this camp was under the jurisdiction of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 57 of this draft version of the statement given this year, the Prosecutor said that on that occasion you said that the person in charge was Milan Gvero, who was in charge of the whole Bijeljina region. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. He was a general, General Gvero, and he is living to this day in Belgrade. I'm quite sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you saw him personally in the command, where was that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: It was in Bijeljina. I went to work there, and the guard would tell us, "Move away from that ramp, because General Milan Gvero is coming." This is how I learned of his name. He was a very large man. And this guy, Serb, told us that he was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like a document to be put before the witness. We have an official English translation attached as well. The document was disclosed to the Prosecution, and it is a memo that was addressed to the committee for exchange in Bijeljina, by the one in Banja Luka, and the document was dated 8th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, just something briefly regarding this document, but I will let you read it first.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Can I get a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that the Prosecution will be able to provide you with one.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, I was supposed to be exchanged on several occasions, and I don't know why that did not materialise. I wasn't exchanged with these people here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic. In the English translation, the first main paragraph, it says -- under investigation, who received abolition. Now, I can see in the B/C/S, there's a word that looks like the B/C/S version of "abolition," but in English it doesn't seem to make any sense to me. Maybe there's another way the B/C/S word should be translated. Perhaps we could find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be best if I read out that first sentence and have it translated by the Court interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a document which, in its heading, indicates that it was sent by the 1st Krajina Corps on the 8th of October, 1993, and it was sent to the committee for exchange of prisoners, personally to the president of that commission, Bodirogic Matija, lieutenant in Bijeljina. The first sentence goes as follows: "We are sending you a list of prisoners who had been convicted or were under investigations, and for them we received pardon, and immediately forwarding it to you for the purposes of tomorrow's arrival." Mr. Bobic, I will read out the third paragraph so that we get some idea about the context. The third paragraph reads as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you go on, can we correct, then, the word "abolition" to read as "pardon" in the English version? Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the third paragraph says as follows: "As regards the changes in the list, the following names can be changed." And then, underneath, you see number 134. Can you read that outloud, please?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. It says Bobic Kemal, son of Salih, 1940, Samac. And then instead of him, Irfan Sabah, son of Mehmed, 1961, Prijedor, can go. And then underneath --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't need to read what's underneath. My question is as follows: Is this your personal data? Does this pertain to you, Kemal Bobic, son of Salih, born in 1940 in Samac? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know, in October of 1993, that you were scheduled to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn that the committee from Tuzla did not request that you be exchanged? It was a Muslim commission from Tuzla. So that commission did not request for you to go into exchange, but rather, Irfan Sabah? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I came after the exchange to Rahic [phoen]. I went there after Sarajevo. I went to the motel called Kobo where the Muslim commission for exchange had its seat, and they told me that they requested me to be exchanged 20 times. And the more they asked for me, the more frequently they were refused. I was even requested by the central commission in Sarajevo, by Amor Masovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not go into that. Let me ask you this: Have you ever heard of Bodirogic Matija, and the other person?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I -- no, I don't know them. Perhaps I saw them while I was in the camp, but, you know, the conditions in the camp were very difficult. The rules were very strict. We were not allowed to talk amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know Sabhaz Irfan [phoen], son of Mehmed? Was he with you in the Batkovici camp?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I think that he came from Manjaca, near Prijedor. Yes, I know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be introduced into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No objection? MR. DI FAZIO: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it marked as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D75/3 and D75/3 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you told us that after you were exchanged you contacted people from the Exchange Commission on the Muslim side, can you then tell whether you know that there were negotiations concerning the exchange of prisoners in Batkovici between military commission headed by Amor Masovic and the military commission of Republika Srpska? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I don't know. All I know is that we were summoned to go to Sarajevo after the exchange. We went to the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that. But let me ask you this first: You spent almost two years in Batkovici. Have you seen other people leave to be exchanged? Did other people from -- not from Samac but from elsewhere come to the camp and later be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. These people were imprisoned with me, and then later on exchanged. They would simply leave the camp, go through the gates, board buses, and leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those were people who were not from Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't really tell, because we couldn't go out, and all we could do is look out from the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will ask you just a few more questions regarding your exchange. You were exchanged in October of 1994, in Sarajevo, as you've told us.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, and I have a document regarding that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please tell me this: Whether you saw Mr. Amor Masovic when you were exchanged. Who is that man? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you know about him?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Everybody, all imprisoned Croats and Muslims and even Serbs know Masovic. There were Serbs imprisoned in the camp with me. Amor Masovic was a man who everybody knew. All three ethnicities were in the camp with me, because they were in the BH army. Amor Masovic was the president of the Exchange Commission, and when I came to be exchanged, at the bridge, we were taken to the tower, and then we came to the brotherhood and unity bridge, where there were Serb positions, and Momcilo Krajisnik came there, there was Asushi Akashi there as well, and then Michael Rose. This is where the delegations negotiated back and forth. And then there were 80-something of us on a bus, and we stayed until 9.00. It was -- we spent the whole night there, and then the first exchange started the following morning, and then I was exchanged in the first exchange. Amor Masovic came in and said, "You will go first."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me just one more thing regarding the exchange: Did anybody there, at the location of the exchange, ask you whether you wanted to go to the other side?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. There was an office. They took us in there, and there were two ladies there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me just one more thing: Do you remember seeing whether soldiers came from the other side and crossed to the territory of Republika Srpska? Did you see people coming from the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I didn't. They exchanged people by numbers. I didn't see Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bobic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bobic. I am Borislav Pisarevic, an attorney representing the defence of Mr. Zaric before this Tribunal. Before I ask any questions, I would like to express, on behalf of Mr. Zaric, his sincere regret for everything that you and your family have experienced and suffered through these unfortunate events in Bosnia and Herzegovina and our municipality of Bosanski Samac. I would also like to ask you to make a short pause before giving your answers, because you already had an opportunity to see what problems ensue if you don't. You and I speak the same language, and I would like to ensure that everything that I and you say is taken in by the Trial Chamber. That's why I would like for you to make a short pause, so that that can be translated. Naturally, everything else that was previously said to you by my colleagues still applies. Mr. Bobic, we shall talk about the time before the 17th of April, 1992, which means that I will ask you some questions which mostly have to do with 1992. You've already told us that you were one of the founders of the SDA. Can we agree that all the members of your family who were of age were also members of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today and yesterday, during your testimony before this Chamber, you said, several times, that you quit the SDA, or rather, I think that you wanted to say that you left the executive board of the SDA. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now tell me the following: When did you leave the executive board of the SDA of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: It was sometime in 1992, at the time of the repeated elections, and then I quit. That is, I stayed in the SDA, but others joined the board. And you know it well. Other men were -- joined the board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that Mr. Sulejman Tihic became the president of the municipal board of the SDA in September 1991, that that was when he was elected to that duty?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because then my conclusion would be right, I think, when I say that from September 1991 were not a member -- that as of that date, you were no longer a member of the executive board of the SDA in the municipality of Samac. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not -- you are not familiar with the activities of the SDA in the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I'm not, because I was -- I no longer attended their meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although you were not a member of the executive board anymore, did you continue to donate funds to the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, I did not donate any money, but they would come to the restaurant to have the meals, to have a dinner. At times they paid, at times they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You must be familiar with the fact that in the municipality of Samac at the time that we are talking about, and that is 1992, all sorts of incidents happened, that there were explosions, sound attacks, barricades, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that, like any other citizen there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you some questions having to do with the 4th Detachment of the JNA, of the 17th Tactical Group, for the simple reason that some questions concerning the 4th Detachment have not been sufficiently clarified during your direct examination before this Chamber by the Prosecution. If I understood you correctly, in your view, and to your knowledge, the 4th Detachment was associated with the party which was called the League of Communists's movement for Yugoslavia. Did I understand that correctly, and is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, it was all written down in Samac. There were posters, movement for Yugoslavia, 4th Detachment, reformist forces, technical group, Ljubisa. Let's not go into it. We know it. No need to put this additional burden on Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, you spoke about the existence of political parties in the municipality of Samac. I did not want to list them all on purpose. Those were parliamentary parties. Can we agree that this movement, that is, this League of Communists movement for Yugoslavia did not exist as a political party in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that. I do not know. I don't have any certain knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that in the 4th Detachment there were many Muslims?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the 4th Detachment of the JNA, in addition to Muslims, there were also members of other ethnicities, those which lived in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, such as Croats, and so on?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: You mean in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Croats and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were various --

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this answer was given yesterday, Mr. Pisarevic. Please try to avoid repeating the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that the 4th Detachment was a military formation within the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, during your testimony, you said, on page 54, line 17, and I quote: "He was something like a commander, the commander of the 4th Detachment." You meant by this, when you said "he," you meant Mr. Simo Zaric, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you said?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. It was all all right and legal, no secret. Mirko [phoen] was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to that. Mr. Bobic, on the 3rd of April, 1998, you gave a statement to the investigators of the OTP of The Hague Tribunal. Do you remember that? Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 3rd of April, 1998.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was an official statement, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed that statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't know if I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody forced you, you didn't do it under duress or anything?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the contents of that statement.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I do not know what statement you mean, because they came, they asked questions, a number of them from the Tribunal, and so on. People came. They have my number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we've referred to this passage before, this statement before. Please go to the direct quotation you want to refer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours. Could the usher please help me to give the witness a copy of his statement of the 3rd of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I want to ask you -- to ask you to find -- to turn to page 3 of the statement. Let me help my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English translation, ERN 60242433 [as interpreted]. Paragraph one before the last. And you will see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Just for the record, so it's all straight, it's not an English translation. The original statement is in English. The original document is the English version, and that is which the witness signed. The translation is the B/C/S. Just so that's clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Go ahead, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is one, two, three, four, five -- fifth passage, the last sentence in that passage. Turn to page 3, Mr. Bobic.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Oh, you've said page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No. You didn't give me the right number. You said 006 something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. This has nothing to do with you. It has to do with my learned friends, and that is a completely different matter. For you, it is page 3, paragraph 5, last sentence in that paragraph. Look at it and I can read it out. You said then: "Simo Zaric was responsible for security, a security officer in the 4th Detachment of the JNA." Did I read correctly what it says?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say this to the investigators of the OTP of The Hague Tribunal on the 3rd of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that you knew at the time that Mr. Zaric was in the 4th Detachment of the JNA and there he was in charge of security matters?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Simo Zaric worked. He was also with the State Security Service. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm speaking about the 4th Detachment as a military formation of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. He was responsible for the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you also knew that Mr. Zaric was not the commander of the 4th Detachment of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: He was the commander and Brko was his deputy. Anybody knew it. I mean, it was all above board. It was all above board. The 4th Detachment, the SDA, and the SDS -- I mean, if that's what you mean, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I want to intervene. The witness said that the 4th Detachment was legal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: At that time. At that time. Before the war, I mean. Before the war, all the parties were lawful. What happened afterwards, we all know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, we need to clarify something here. We are not talking about whether the parties were lawful. We are not talking about whether Yugoslav People's Army was legal. Can you distinguish between political parties, on the one hand, and the Yugoslav People's Army, that is, the 4th Detachment, as an institution of the defence of the then state?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know how to explain, because I was never amongst the political leadership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying you do not know?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this statement that you gave to the OTP, which you have in front of you -- keep it for a while, because I wish to remind you of your testimony yesterday, when, on page 55, lines 5 to 7 of the transcript, you said: "Naser told me that I was to go to the SUP because Simo Zaric had ordered that I be taken in for interview."

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: That is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated this?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few questions. This Naser, as a matter of fact, is policeman Naser Sejdic, called Cakar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in incident that you mentioned happened on the 23rd of May, 1992; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: 23rd of May, 1992, not -- oh, yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now will you turn to page 4 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For our learned friends, it is the original of the statement 00602435, second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For you, it is paragraph 7. It begins on the 23rd of May. So will you please read this first sentence, if it presents no problem to you.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: You mean "on the 23rd of May"? Is that what you want me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: On the 23rd of May, 1992, Naser Sejdic (a policeman I mentioned earlier) came to my place with two Serbs and took me to the police station. There were 20 or so citizens more --"

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't have to go further, but we went through this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The record is not clear. Mr. Pisarevic, the record is not clear, because the witness read so fast. Can you read it, slowly, so that we have it on record clearly?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, it says: "On the 23rd of May, 1992, Naser Sejdic (a policeman whom I mentioned earlier) came to my house with two Serbs and took me to the police station." Did I read correctly what is written here?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bobic, you still stand by the statement which you gave on the 3rd of April, 1998, to the investigators of the OTP of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: You mean this statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I do stand by it. Why? This is all correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is all correct?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, it is. If you want me to help somebody with something, that's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's correct the transcript. It should be April 1998? That's the year you mentioned, April 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 1998. 3rd of April, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Bobic, in your testimony, you said how Simo Zaric was present in the office with Stevo Todorovic, Perica Krstanovic, Predrag Adzic, when you were brought to Stevan Todorovic's office for the second time. That is what you said yesterday. During your conversation with Mr. Zaric, and in preparation for this examination, Mr. Zaric affirms that it is not true that he -- that in Stevan Todorovic's office he was ever with Stevan Todorovic, Perica Krstanovic, Predrag Adzic, and that he never saw you there.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: May I answer? Why would I be lying about that? The answer is no, which means he was in the office. Simo knows it. He knows it well. It's nothing dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned somebody called Pero Kitic, and you explained how you came to know him and so on. Mr. Bobic, I read your statement of the 3rd of April, 1998, carefully, and established that in that statement you never once mention Mr. Pero Kitic or the events in which he played a part. Do you remember mentioning it or not?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I merely answered the questions that the Tribunal asked me. What they asked me, I answered. Perhaps it never got to that, but this man saved my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. So we can agree that you did not mention him because you were not -- because the investigators never asked you about him or about the events related to him?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Mr. Kitic stayed with you that day, that he stayed on for lunch at your place, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that meeting, after that day - and that was sometime in early May - did you ever see Mr. Kitic again?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him in the shop, because there was this order that all the publicans had to keep their outlets open, so I did. He came, Pero Kitic came there and sat down for a while, had a drink, and he was sleeping at Simo Zaric's, in his house. That is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, but we'll have to clear it up a bit. So in early May, after your first meeting with Pero Kitic, you met again several times?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, two, maybe three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that you saw him in your restaurant called Sedrvan? You are aware that Mr. Kitic spent nights at Fadil Topcagic's; don't you know it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. That is what he told me, and I saw him come from there, because the shop was in between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on those occasions when you were together, in May 1992, did you also play chess?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Kitic was killed?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your restaurant, Sedrvan, was not damaged, therefore, whilst you were free?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: It wasn't, no. It was quite all right, except that the glass was broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was the glass broken?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it due to -- a result of the detonation?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that your coffee bar, Sedrvan, was considerably damaged when it was hit by rocket launchers and that your neighbour, Fikret Omeragic [phoen] was killed?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Fiktet Omeragic you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Fikret Omeragic was killed on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: It was some three or four days after the war broke out in Samac. I don't know. I can't remember. He died in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know at all whether your restaurant, Sedrvan, was ever hit by a shell or a rocket which landed on your cafe or nearby?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Well, how could I know something like that? I was in camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of it?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I heard. Muric's [phoen] wife came to visit. She was a Serb, and she told me that Sedrvan had been destroyed. That was sometime in 1993 or early 1994. I never asked anybody as to the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll put a few more questions to you and then we will finish shortly. I'll ask you a few things about Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we can a break for 20 minutes? We'll continue at 1250 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You're continuing your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, just before we broke off, I told you that we would talk about Mr. Zaric. You know Mr. Zaric well, don't you? Can you please speak up?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know his family well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, because my relative is an aunt of his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that Mr. Zaric was a decent and prominent citizen of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. Before I war I did not have a bad opinion of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please confirm to us that Mr. Zaric, Mr. Sarkanovic, Mr. Simandic, and Pisarevic, Mihajlo Topolovac, so with all of those people he came to your house on the 14th of February, 1992, to express his condolences after your son was killed? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that after your son was killed, in Samac, in the cinema, a gathering of citizens was held, and it was devoted to the safety, security, of all of the residents in Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear somebody speak afterwards about that rally or gathering of residents, where security issues were discussed? Do you remember somebody telling you that Simo Zaric spoke at that gathering as well?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I can't remember. At the time, I was building my shop, so I didn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question I mean to ask you pertains to the restitution of your property. You have mentioned Mr. Milos Savic here, who is the president of the Court in Samac, and who allowed for that judgement to be enforced.

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That Milos Savic is the same person who, before the war, meaning in 1992, used to work in the public security station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have concluded, Mr. Bobic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you Re-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions this morning by the first Defence counsel, Mr. Vukovic, regarding the arming of the SDA and the arming of the population, and indeed a passage was put to you from paragraph 8 of your draft statement prepared in June of this year. I want to read paragraph 8 to you and ask you if you agree that that is the paragraph that was put into the draft statement: "In my opinion, the non-Serb citizens in Bosanski Samac were not generally armed. The Muslims in the town did not have money for firearms. As far as I know, some of the population had hunting rifles with permits, but there was no campaign to arm the population and the SDA -- and the population, and the SDA in the area were not involved in supplying weapons to its members. There had been some discussion in the SDA party as to whether we should try and get arms because of the war in Croatia and the activity of the JNA and information that the Serbs were being armed. In particular, the Serbs had built up military equipment and weapons in the village of Obudovac, which is 18 kilometres away from Bosanski Samac town. However, I was personally against arming. I heard that Alija Fitozovic may have bought weapons in Croatia, but I know nothing about it." Is that the paragraph that you had in your draft statement provided in June of this year?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with the contents, with what is contained in that paragraph that I've just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness have Exhibit D49/1 ter ID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please take this and tell them that I know nothing of this? This is my handwriting, and this is a forged one. I know nothing of this. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that that's your position. I understand that. I've heard your evidence. I understand that you say that that's not your statement. No problem. I understand that. I just want you to read out a paragraph of it, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake -- if I may. Sorry, my learned friend. So the sake of clarity and for the transcript, could we, according to the words that the witness just said, on page 74, line 5 until 7, to know exactly for the record to which document this witness makes certain reference that it's forgery? Because it's not clear from his words here. Obviously he took a look on two documents, but we don't know exactly about what document he is speaking. Just just for the record, with references to these words on page 74 and line 5 and 7. Could we clarify that? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that. If Your Honours please, I don't propose to put anything from that document to the witness, but I will now clarify the query that Mr. Pantelic has raised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on reflection, I'm not going to ask you anything about the content of the document, but D49/1 ter ID, the document that you say is not yours, you referred to a forgery just a moment ago. Were you there talking about that very document dated the 16th of March, 1998, the document that the Court has marked D49/1 ter ID?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: I was simply saying that this signature here is not mine, and you can see my original signature on another document. You can compare it on Internet. And everything that I have stated to this Tribunal is accurate. I would just like for you to take a look at this, for the purposes of your record, and to establish that this here is a forgery. This is what they, the other people, gave me. This is what my signature looks like as recorded in the municipal books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, the witness has demonstrated and commented on that issue and has provided a new document in which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which new document? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, it's another document. As you can see on the -- does Your Honour have the ELMO switched on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, but are you accepting it? Is it of any use your case? MR. DI FAZIO: No, it's not. I mean, I don't want to use it. The witness did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So he has no instructions to produce another document, so you had better withdraw it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Very well. I'll deal with it in that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we forget about D49/1 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise again, Your Honour. In spite of my efforts to see from his previous answer that he is specifically speaking about D49/1 ter ID. Since this person is a layperson, maybe it's a misunderstanding. Just for the record, could we put on the ELMO and then hear a confirmation from the Prosecution that this witness said that document D49/1 ter ID, with the Prosecution ERN numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- is a forgery. That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That has been done. It's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So it's not -- could I hear from the Prosecution that's not in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This witness made a reference to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is on record. It's clear that he referred to D49/1 ter ID. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. Can we move on now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said in evidence that you had received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher go and sit? Because you're no longer referring to that document. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that you received bread and milk. How long did that go on for after the 16th and 17th of April, the receipt of bread and milk?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Some two to three days. Yes. We received it for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any supplies of bread and milk again up until the time that you were arrested and detained?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive anything. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. The topic of a gift of property of yours was raised by counsel, and there was reference to a gift made to a Gordana Pavlovic, who was the daughter - sorry - the girlfriend of one of your sons. What ethnic background was she?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: A Serb. She was of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to go into the details of the case or documentation related to her, or anything. Can you just tell us, pure and simple: Did you ever want to give your son's girlfriend part of your property? Did you ever intend to do that?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me? I think I may have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just one last issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions about the role of Mr. Zaric in the 4th Detachment, and there was reference to his being a security officer. In your statement of the 3rd of April, 1998, when you were discussing your knowledge of defendants in this case, did you say that Simo Zaric was the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: On page 77, line 2, the question reads as follows: "Did you ever see any supplies of bread and milk again up until the time that you were arrested and detained?" Was the intention with that question to ask whether he did receive milk and bread, or if there was distributed milk and bread around the city? Because if I have understood correctly, he probably had some supplies of his own, as owner of a restaurant. So I think you should make a distinction between those two questions. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand what Your Honour's concern is. Perhaps I'll clarify it, if I may, with the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us already that you received bread and milk in the first few days and then it stopped and you didn't receive any bread and milk thereafter, at least up until the time that you were arrested. Are you aware of supplies of bread and milk being distributed to every section, all ethnic groups in the population, in the period of time up until your arrest?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: Bread and milk were distributed only for some two or three days, so that people would not leave Samac and so that they could see who had remained in Samac. It was a political trap. It was no assistance whatsoever. I naturally had a lot of supplies, food supplies, in my own house, which could sustain me for a year. I had my own supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct from that last answer that the distribution of bread and milk stopped permanently and it was never done again, to anyone, at least up until the time that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: "Did you, on the 12th of March, give any statement?"  I'm just
utterances.text: No. Nobody received anything after some two or three days. If one had money, one could go and get it, but the shelling was already going on and people were not moving about a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bobic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now released. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have witnesses, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I regret to say that no, we don't, if Your Honours please. The next witness is a protected witness, and I believe it's Witness P. But in any event, this man is working in a nearby European country, and arrangements were made some time ago for him to be -- to go to Croatia and from a place in Croatia to fly to The Hague, and that will occur, but it will occur on the weekend. And so we don't have any other available witnesses. That is, I submit, a quite unusual event. Generally the Prosecution has been pretty good in having witnesses on time. We didn't expect that both Mr. And Mrs. Bobic would complete their evidence in quite the sort of period of time that they have, and I think the Chamber might agree that certainly as far as their examination-in-chief was concerned -- it set records for speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's okay. What other witnesses do we have remaining? MR. DI FAZIO: They're all protected witnesses at this stage, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can go into closed session. I mean private session and deal with this. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
